extracted.intended_audience: improv students and instructors at The Second City (or similar comedy schools)
extracted.subtask_description: A teaching/evaluation framework for improvised scene work and sketch creation used in Second City classes, focused on ensemble play, character-based choices, and sketch joke structure. Intended to guide instructors and students when creating, rehearsing, and assessing improv and sketch scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes, And
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundational concept introduced in Improv 1: acceptance + collaborative idea-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always agree, then add. Use acceptance to build scenes rather than block. (Page wording: 'Foundational concept introduced in Improv 1. Acceptance + collaborative idea-building. Always agree, then add.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble (group over individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize the ensemble over individual performances; the group outcome matters more than individual moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize collaboration and collective support rather than seeking personal spotlight. Appears as a Spolin fundamental and as an explicit rubric question ('Is the ensemble prioritized over individuals?'). Also reinforced in Sketch Creation Principles: 'Collaboration > solo writing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Object work
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mime and convincing physicalization of objects to create believable, specific scene reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice miming objects with conviction as part of Spolin Fundamentals to ground scenes physically and support partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (specific where)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a specific environment—a clear 'where'—to anchor the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete about the scene location and physical context to provide constraints and detail that fuel choices and comedy ('Environment (specific where)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Sidecoaching (gentle guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use gentle, in-the-moment coaching to guide performers without taking over the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors should offer subtle corrections or prompts (sidecoaching) rather than direct intervention; supports learning while keeping scenes live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being in the Moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pre-planning; react to what just happened and trust scene partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't pre-plan. React to what just happened. Trust scene partners. Evaluation looks for performers who listen and respond spontaneously rather than executing rehearsed beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Point of View (POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each player has a clear point of view that drives consistent choices throughout the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POV should inform behavior and generate comedic choices: 'Each player has a clear point of view. POV drives consistent choices. POV makes scenes fertile for comedy.' Assess whether characters make choices true to their POV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating from Abundance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer many ideas; do not withhold—specific choices are better than safe ones and performers should play full out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't withhold; offer many ideas. Specific is better than safe. Play full out. Scoring favors quantity and specificity of offers that create options for the scene rather than minimal or tentative contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Structure (in Sketch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply classic joke architecture in sketch writing: setup → twist → punch, with an emphasis on the scene's 'game'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch comedy uses the same improv principles but structures them: 'Setup → twist → punch.' Recognize the 'game of the scene' (UCB-influenced) and build layered joke structure on that game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game of the Scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and heighten the recurring comedic pattern or 'game' that defines the scene's humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to joke structure and sketch work; the 'game' is the pattern to be found and exploited. Influence noted as UCB-influenced. Evaluate whether the scene discovers and plays the game's pattern effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration over Solo Writing (Sketch Creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer collaborative sketch creation and group-generated material rather than solo-written pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Collaboration > solo writing.' Assess rehearsal and creation processes for collaborative input and ensemble authorship rather than isolated authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-Driven Sketch Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Let character development drive the comedy; build joke structure layered on character truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character development should be the source of comedic situations: 'Character development drives comedy.' 'Joke structure layered on character truth'—evaluate whether jokes arise organically from character choices rather than imposed gags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second City Style Rubric Questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise checklist used for quick evaluation of scenes: Are players 'yes-and-ing'? Is the ensemble prioritized? Is each character given a specific POV? Are players in the moment? Are choices specific and abundant?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these five diagnostic questions as an at-a-glance rubric for classes and rehearsals to determine whether core principles are present. They summarize and operationalize the teaching philosophy for practical assessment.
